title: Invocation ontology mapper and backfill shim
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We support two primary invocation paradigms: OpenAI-style tool declarations (name + JSON schema + description) and our older 'legacy functions' (positional/keyword args, protobuf-like signatures). Customers integrate both simultaneously and expect predictable behavior when a model selects a tool/function. Current edge cases: name collisions, nested argument shapes, streaming partial outputs, and telemetry gaps that make post-hoc disambiguation hard.

Goal: Implement an 'ontology mapper' at the API gateway/runtime boundary that: (1) canonicalizes invocation names and aliases; (2) performs argument shape translation between OpenAI tool schemas and legacy function signatures; (3) provides a low-latency shim that can backfill / re-interpret recent historical invocations for analytics and migration; (4) enriches telemetry and confidence metadata so rollouts and fallbacks are observable. The shim must be incremental, safe by default, and support canary rollout with automatic fallback to legacy behavior on errors.
acceptance_criteria: API can map an OpenAI-style tool declaration to an equivalent legacy function signature at runtime with <5ms median extra latency for simple mappings
Argument translators handle nested objects and arrays for 90% of identified customer schemas (based on sample corpus) without user intervention
Backfill shim can reprocess last 30 days of invocations for a single customer in under 2 hours (for analytics and migration reporting)
Telemetry includes: mapping version, confidence score, applied transformations, and fallback reason when used
Canary rollout policy supports per-customer toggle, with automatic rollback on error-rate regression >0.5% above baseline
Security review completed and secrets/PII paths validated before GA
design_decisions: Use a layered approach: name resolution -> schema alignment -> argument adapter -> invocation proxy
Maintain a small canonical registry (in Redis) of name aliases and preferred canonical names; runtime can query with TTL cache
Translate arguments using declarative transform specs (JSONPath + simple ops) stored in a versioned store; runtime falls back to inference heuristics when transform not present
Expose transformation metadata in response 'invocation_meta' and to Console traces for cost/latency dashboards
Streaming: do not buffer streaming tool outputs to apply transforms; instead apply best-effort pass-through transforms and mark output as 'partial' until final chunk
Backfill: implement a worker that replays recorded request/response pairs into the mapper in analysis mode (no external side effects); record diffs for migration reports
implementation_notes: Gateway change only: introduce a new handler 'invocation-ontology' that can be toggled per-customer
Add a lightweight transform DSL (v0) supporting rename, flatten, map-array, coerce-type, and default-values
Default alias heuristics: lowercasing + punctuation-normalization + fuzzy-match (edit distance <=2) with telemetry tag when heuristic used
For functions with required positional args, attempt to compile OpenAI-style object args into positional order using signature metadata; fail-open to keyword style if ambiguous
Limit worst-case mapping latency by capping heuristic resolution attempts and returning 'needs-manual-mapping' in invocation_meta
runtime_algorithm_outline: 1) Resolve name: check canonical registry -> exact match -> alias list -> heuristic fuzzy match
2) Load target signature/schema from model catalog or legacy function registry
3) Match input payload to schema: attempt direct validation -> attempt transforms -> mark confidence
4) If streaming: forward chunks, tag first chunk with invocation_meta and confidence; mark final chunk with full transform report
5) If transform not possible and 'strict' per-customer setting is true -> return 422 with guidance link; else call legacy endpoint with original payload and mark fallback
6) Log mapping decision and minimal diff to datastore for backfill/query
testing_plan: Unit tests for transform DSL: rename, flatten, array-map, type coercions
Integration tests: replay 1000 real invocation traces (anonymized) through mapper and assert semantic equivalence or documented fallback
Load test: synthetic traffic simulating 50k invocations/min to ensure mapper latency P99 <= 200ms added overhead in worst-case heuristics
Canary: stagger on 2 internal customers then 5 beta customers, monitor error, latency, and 'needs-manual-mapping' rate
Security test: verify no transform path leaks customer-provided secrets into logs; run static analysis on transform templates
migration_and_rollout: Phase 0 (alpha): internal-only toggle for Redwood teams; iterate on transform DSL and registry
Phase 1 (canary): enable per-customer toggle for 7 beta customers; monitor rollback signals
Phase 2 (gradual): opt-in for self-serve customers via Console toggle and API flag; provide migration report
Phase 3 (GA): default-on for new customers; opt-out for existing customers for 3 months before forced migration
Provide a Console page that shows mapping diffs, confidence histograms, and suggested manual transforms

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Heuristic mapping mis-invocations could trigger incorrect customer actions. Mitigation: default to safe fallback (no transform) for low-confidence matches and surface suggested mapping to Console
Risk: Backfill worker could generate high I/O load when reprocessing large customers. Mitigation: rate-limit workers per-customer and support scheduling windows
Risk: Transform DSL could be abused to exfiltrate secrets into logs. Mitigation: static analysis + runtime scrubber + limited built-in ops (no arbitrary JS)
notes_for_reviewers: Focus review on (1) transform DSL security constraints, (2) streaming partial-transform semantics, and (3) telemetry fields required for Console integration. Provide explicit acceptance criteria edits if any metric thresholds should be tightened.
estimate_reasoning: 8 points: 3 for DSL and registry, 2 for runtime mapping and instrumentation, 2 for backfill worker prototype, 1 for tests and canary plumbing
